text:
Vegas had the best and worst of its week inside 72 hours. On Tuesday the Golden Knights beat Edmonton 5-3 behind two goals each from Jack Eichel and rookie Trevor Connelly, a win the Las Vegas Review-Journal called "signature." On Friday they lost 4-1 in San Jose, their first regulation loss at SAP Center in franchise history, per Sharks Hockey Digest. Neither night changes much. This is a good team having a normal November.

The numbers back that up. Vegas is 15-7-5 and gets 54.7% of the expected goals, among the best in the West, and has scored about six fewer goals than its chances deserve. Mark Stone, who set a franchise scoring record this month and whom NHL.com called the "epitome of being a Golden Knight," is part of that: 4 points in his last 10 games on 9.5 expected. His line with Eichel and Ivan Barbashev has 59% of the expected goals and a 10-4 goal edge, so the points should come. Adin Hill has been better than his save percentage shows, 3.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

Connelly, who leads all rookies in points according to Jesse Granger of The Athletic, is the new piece. The concerns sit lower in the lineup: the Nic Dowd checking line is at 37% of the expected goals, and Rasmus Andersson with Jeremy Lauzon at 41% and outscored 15-7.

Our numbers give Vegas a 97% chance at the playoffs and 54% at the division. What we'd watch: whether that second pair holds up in a tight Pacific race.
